pages.title: A shared section across different uses
pages.body: Table and floor lights share a linear body, luminous strips and distinctive ends. Support, length and direction change around the use scenario.

images.caption: Silver table lamp with a circular base beside an open book on a blue surface
Full view of a silver floor lamp against black

pages.title: Separate material and functional cues
pages.body: Metal channels, luminous surfaces and circular controls explain different roles. Renderings support comparison of reflection and proportion; optical performance requires testing.

images.caption: Detail of a gold light body with longitudinal light strips and a circular control
Horizontal pendant with parallel light strips, metal channels and end details against a dark background

pages.title: Check the object against the room
pages.body: Wall recesses and long tables provide scale references. Scenes help compare length, mounting and visual centre in an actual use context.

images.caption: Gold vertical wall light within a grey architectural recess
Horizontal linear pendant above a dining table and chairs

pages.title: Turn a child’s use into form constraints
pages.body: Sketches and physical models explore grip, mouthpiece position and approachability. Clinical performance and manufacture remain outside the validated scope.

images.caption: Sketches, handmade form models and AIGC exploration

pages.title: Separate contact, grip and charging
pages.body: Mouth contact, handheld volume and charging base have different requirements. Their separation makes the relationship between position and action available for review.

pages.title: Connect the product and its feedback
pages.body: The device and base form a use unit. Interface feedback addresses children, carers and clinicians. Models and renderings document the concept stage.

images.caption: Proposed breath interaction and feedback sequence

pages.title: From travel preparation to maintenance
pages.body: Carrying, changing modules, cleaning and storage create different tasks. The journey gives the product system concrete design criteria.

pages.title: Organise the system around use
pages.body: The handle, replaceable modules and supporting information respond to carrying, switching, cleaning and storage. The diagram analyses original concept evidence.

pages.title: Connect the object and its instructions
pages.body: The companion interface organises care guidance and module recognition. Naming, colour and hierarchy remain consistent across the product and instructions.

pages.title: Define the roles before the equipment
pages.body: The service blueprint separates public participation, professional operation and equipment maintenance. Permissions and information flows frame the scanning, transport and return tasks.

pages.title: Explain the robot through its parts
pages.body: Overall and exploded views connect the body, actuators and tail. This concept does not establish sealing, power or pipe-traversal performance.

pages.title: Connect equipment and interface
pages.body: The station, device and control interface support parking, execution and monitoring. Their relationship makes it possible to review entry, feedback and recovery.
